1	"""HTTP server exposing the ledger REST API using the Python standard library."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import json
5	from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
6	from urllib.parse import parse_qs, unquote
7	
8	from .service import LedgerService
9	
10	MAX_BODY_BYTES = 1 << 20  # 1 MiB cap on request bodies
11	
12	
13	def build_handler(service: LedgerService) -> type[BaseHTTPRequestHandler]:
14	    """Create a handler class closed over the given ledger service."""
15	
16	    class LedgerHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
17	        server_version = "VerifiableLedger/1.0"
18	
19	        # -- helpers --------------------------------------------------------
20	
21	        def _send_json(self, status: int, body: dict) -> None:
22	            data = json.dumps(body, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
23	            self.send_response(status)
24	            self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
25	            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
26	            self.end_headers()
27	            self.wfile.write(data)
28	
29	        def _read_json(self) -> tuple[bool, object]:
30	            try:
31	                length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
32	            except ValueError:
33	                return False, {"error": "invalid Content-Length"}
34	            if length <= 0:
35	                return False, {"error": "request body must be JSON"}
36	            if length > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
37	                return False, {"error": "request body too large"}
38	            raw = self.rfile.read(length)
39	            try:
40	                return True, json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
41	            except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
42	                return False, {"error": "request body must be valid JSON"}
43	
44	        # -- routing --------------------------------------------------------
45	
46	        def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 (stdlib naming)
47	            path = self.path.split("?", 1)[0]
48	            if path == "/v1/transactions":
49	                ok, payload = self._read_json()
50	                if not ok:
51	                    self._send_json(400, payload)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
52	                    return
53	                status, body = service.submit_transaction(payload)
54	                self._send_json(status, body)
55	            elif path == "/v1/forks/candidates":
56	                ok, payload = self._read_json()
57	                if not ok:
58	                    self._send_json(400, payload)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
59	                    return
60	                status, body = service.submit_fork_candidate(payload)
61	                self._send_json(status, body)
62	            elif path == "/v1/forks/sync":
63	                ok, payload = self._read_json()
64	                if not ok:
65	                    self._send_json(400, payload)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
66	                    return
67	                status, body = service.submit_fork_sync(payload)
68	                self._send_json(status, body)
69	            elif path == "/v1/trust/sources":
70	                # POST /v1/trust/sources — register a trusted source.
71	                ok, payload = self._read_json()
72	                if not ok:
73	                    self._send_json(400, payload)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
74	                    return
75	                status, body = service.register_trust_source(payload)
76	                self._send_json(status, body)
77	            elif (
78	                path.startswith("/v1/trust/sources/")
79	                and (path.endswith("/rotate") or path.endswith("/revoke"))
80	            ):
81	                # POST /v1/trust/sources/{source}/rotate | /revoke
82	                ok, payload = self._read_json()
83	                if not ok:
84	                    self._send_json(400, payload)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
85	                    return
86	                remainder = path[len("/v1/trust/sources/") :]
87	                if remainder.endswith("/rotate"):
88	                    source = unquote(remainder[: -len("/rotate")])
89	                    status, body = service.rotate_trust_source(source, payload)
90	                else:
91	                    source = unquote(remainder[: -len("/revoke")])
92	                    status, body = service.revoke_trust_source(source, payload)
93	                self._send_json(status, body)
94	            elif path.startswith("/v1/forks/") and path.endswith("/adopt"):
95	                # POST /v1/forks/{tip_hash}/adopt — a body is not required.
96	                if self.headers.get("Content-Length"):
97	                    self._read_json()
98	                tip_hash = unquote(path[len("/v1/forks/") : -len("/adopt")])
99	                status, body = service.adopt_fork(tip_hash)
100	                self._send_json(status, body)
101	            elif path == "/v1/blocks":
102	                # A body is not required; drain one if present.
103	                if self.headers.get("Content-Length"):
104	                    self._read_json()
105	                status, body = service.mine_block()
106	                self._send_json(status, body)
107	            elif path.startswith("/v1/blocks/"):
108	                remainder = path[len("/v1/blocks/") :]
109	                # POST /v1/blocks/{height}/confirm | /v1/blocks/{height}/rollback
110	                if self.headers.get("Content-Length"):
111	                    self._read_json()
112	                if remainder.endswith("/confirm"):
113	                    height = unquote(remainder[: -len("/confirm")])
114	                    status, body = service.confirm_block(height)
115	                elif remainder.endswith("/rollback"):
116	                    height = unquote(remainder[: -len("/rollback")])
117	                    status, body = service.rollback_block(height)
118	                else:
119	                    status, body = 404, {"error": "not found"}
120	                self._send_json(status, body)
121	            else:
122	                self._send_json(404, {"error": "not found"})
123	
124	        def do_GET(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 (stdlib naming)
125	            path, _, query = self.path.partition("?")
126	            if path == "/v1/trust":
127	                status, body = service.get_trust_document()
128	                self._send_json(status, body)
129	            elif path == "/v1/audit/events":
130	                # GET /v1/audit/events?source=&kind=&cursor=&limit=
131	                params = {
132	                    key: values[0]
133	                    for key, values in parse_qs(query, keep_blank_values=True).items()
134	                }
135	                status, body = service.list_audit_events(params)
136	                self._send_json(status, body)
137	            elif path == "/v1/chain":
138	                status, body = service.get_chain()
139	                self._send_json(status, body)
140	            elif path == "/v1/forks/sync":
141	                # GET /v1/forks/sync?source=&min_height=&max_height=&limit=&cursor=
142	                params = {
143	                    key: values[0]
144	                    for key, values in parse_qs(query, keep_blank_values=True).items()
145	                }
146	                status, body = service.list_fork_syncs(params)
147	                self._send_json(status, body)
148	            elif path == "/v1/index/transactions":
149	                # GET /v1/index/transactions?tx_id=&account=&height=&limit=&cursor=
150	                params = {
151	                    key: values[0]
152	                    for key, values in parse_qs(query, keep_blank_values=True).items()
153	                }
154	                status, body = service.list_transactions(params)
155	                self._send_json(status, body)
156	            elif path.startswith("/v1/forks/") and path.endswith("/export"):
157	                # GET /v1/forks/{tip_hash}/export
158	                tip_hash = unquote(path[len("/v1/forks/") : -len("/export")])
159	                status, body = service.export_fork(tip_hash)
160	                self._send_json(status, body)
161	            elif path.startswith("/v1/blocks/"):
162	                remainder = path[len("/v1/blocks/") :]
163	                if "/proof/" in remainder:
164	                    # GET /v1/blocks/{height}/proof/{tx_id}
165	                    height_raw, tx_raw = remainder.split("/proof/", 1)
166	                    if not height_raw or not tx_raw:
167	                        self._send_json(404, {"error": "not found"})
168	                        return
169	                    status, body = service.get_proof(unquote(height_raw), unquote(tx_raw))
170	                    self._send_json(status, body)
171	                elif remainder.endswith("/status"):
172	                    # GET /v1/blocks/{height}/status
173	                    height = unquote(remainder[: -len("/status")])
174	                    status, body = service.get_block_status(height)
175	                    self._send_json(status, body)
176	                else:
177	                    height = unquote(remainder)
178	                    status, body = service.get_block(height)
179	                    self._send_json(status, body)
180	            elif path.startswith("/v1/accounts/"):
181	                account = unquote(path[len("/v1/accounts/") :])
182	                if not account:
183	                    self._send_json(404, {"error": "account not found"})
184	                    return
185	                status, body = service.get_account(account)
186	                self._send_json(status, body)
187	            else:
188	                self._send_json(404, {"error": "not found"})
189	
190	    return LedgerHandler
191	
192	
193	def serve(service: LedgerService, host: str, port: int) -> ThreadingHTTPServer:
194	    """Create and run the HTTP server (blocks until interrupted)."""
195	    httpd = ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), build_handler(service))
196	    httpd.serve_forever()
197	    return httpd

1	"""Ledger business logic: submit transactions, mine blocks, query state,
2	and drive the confirm/rollback block state machine.
3	
4	Block lifecycle
5	---------------
6	The genesis block is born ``confirmed``. Mining (POST /v1/blocks) is only
7	allowed when the chain tip is confirmed and the mempool is non-empty; it
8	produces a ``pending`` block. A pending tip can then be *confirmed* (making
9	its transactions count toward balances and proofs) or *rolled back* (the
10	block is deleted and its transactions return to the mempool de-duplicated).
11	Only the tip can ever be pending, so a confirmed block is final.
12	
13	Balance convention
14	------------------
15	The contract defines no minting endpoint, so every identity starts with a
16	fixed endowment (``initial_balance``, overridable via LEDGER_INITIAL_BALANCE).
17	An account's confirmed balance is::
18	
19	    initial_balance + sum(confirmed amounts received) - sum(confirmed amounts sent)
20	
21	Only confirmed blocks count. The reported balance additionally subtracts the
22	account's spends sitting in the pending (unconfirmed) tip block — pending
23	*credits* are deliberately not counted. An identity only becomes a *queryable
24	account* once it appears in a confirmed block; GET account before that
25	returns 404. Balance checks at submission time treat an identity that has
26	never appeared on chain as holding the initial endowment, otherwise the first
27	transaction in an empty ledger could never be accepted.
28	"""
29	from __future__ import annotations
30	
31	import hashlib
32	import json
33	import time
34	
35	from . import crypto
36	from .models import STATUS_CONFIRMED, STATUS_PENDING, Block, Transaction
37	from .store import TRUST_ACTIVE, TRUST_REVOKED, LedgerStore
38	
39	DEFAULT_INITIAL_BALANCE = 1_000_000
40	
41	REQUIRED_TX_FIELDS = ("from", "to", "amount", "signature")
42	
43	# Audit event kinds. The log is append-only: trust lifecycle changes
44	# (registered/rotated/revoked) and inter-node sync events
45	# (received/adopted/expired) are all recorded permanently.
46	EVENT_SOURCE_REGISTERED = "source_registered"
47	EVENT_SOURCE_ROTATED = "source_rotated"
48	EVENT_SOURCE_REVOKED = "source_revoked"
49	EVENT_SYNC_RECEIVED = "sync_received"
50	EVENT_SYNC_ADOPTED = "sync_adopted"
51	EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED = "sync_expired"
52	
53	
54	def _parse_height(height: object) -> int | None:
55	    """Strict decimal height parse; None when malformed."""
56	    try:
57	        height_int = int(height)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
58	        if str(height_int) != str(height).strip():
59	            raise ValueError
60	        return height_int
61	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
62	        return None

94	    def submit_transaction(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
95	        """Validate and enqueue a transaction. Returns (status, body)."""
96	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
97	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
98	        for field in REQUIRED_TX_FIELDS:
99	            if field not in payload:
100	                return 400, {"error": f"missing field: {field}"}
101	
102	        sender = payload["from"]
103	        recipient = payload["to"]
104	        amount = payload["amount"]
105	        signature = payload["signature"]
106	
107	        if not isinstance(sender, str) or not sender:
108	            return 400, {"error": "field 'from' must be a non-empty string"}
109	        if not isinstance(recipient, str) or not recipient:
110	            return 400, {"error": "field 'to' must be a non-empty string"}
111	        # bool is a subclass of int: reject it and all non-int types explicitly.
112	        if not isinstance(amount, int) or isinstance(amount, bool) or amount <= 0:
113	            return 400, {"error": "field 'amount' must be a positive integer"}
114	        if not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature:
115	            return 400, {"error": "field 'signature' must be a non-empty string"}
116	
117	        message = crypto.canonical_message(sender, recipient, amount)
118	        if not crypto.verify_signature(sender, message, signature):
119	            return 400, {"error": "invalid signature"}
120	
121	        tx = Transaction(sender, recipient, amount, signature)
122	        with self.store.lock:
123	            if tx.tx_id in self.store.pending:
124	                return 409, {"error": "transaction already pending", "tx_id": tx.tx_id}
125	            if any(tx.tx_id == existing.tx_id for block in self.store.chain for existing in block.transactions):
126	                return 409, {"error": "transaction already confirmed", "tx_id": tx.tx_id}
127	            if self.available_balance(sender) < amount:
128	                return 400, {"error": "insufficient balance"}
129	            self.store.pending[tx.tx_id] = tx
130	            try:
131	                self.store.save()
132	            except BaseException:
133	                # Persistence failed: drop the in-memory enqueue so memory
134	                # keeps matching the last durably committed state.
135	                self.store.pending.pop(tx.tx_id, None)
136	                raise
137	        return 202, {"tx_id": tx.tx_id}

145	        the pending tip until it is confirmed or rolled back.

200	        Confirming an already-confirmed block is idempotent (200); every
201	        other case — unknown or malformed height, non-tip pending block —
202	        returns 409.

209	            if block is None:
210	                return 409, {"error": "block cannot be confirmed"}
211	            if block.status == STATUS_CONFIRMED:

213	                return 200, {"height": block.height, "status": STATUS_CONFIRMED}
214	            if block is not self.store.tip():
215	                return 409, {"error": "only the chain tip can be confirmed"}

218	                return 409, {"error": "previous block is not confirmed"}
219	            block.status = STATUS_CONFIRMED
220	            try:
221	                self.store.save()

231	        height) return 404; a confirmed block or a non-tip block returns 409.

314	        be rolled back, so it must not inflate the reported balance.

328	        counted, so a sequence of submissions cannot spend money that has not
329	        been confirmed yet.

339	    @staticmethod
340	    def _fork_summary(blocks: list) -> dict:
341	        """Public fork descriptor S: tip_hash, height, length, status."""
342	        tip = blocks[-1]

344	            "tip_hash": tip.block_hash,

351	    def _winning_fork(self) -> tuple[str, list]:
352	        """Pick the winner among the canonical chain and every candidate.
353	
354	        Longest chain wins; equal lengths are broken by the smallest tip hash
355	        (lexicographic hex order). Returns (tip_hash, block list).
356	        """
357	        contenders: list[tuple[str, list]] = [
358	            (self.store.tip_hash(), self.store.chain)
359	        ]
360	        contenders.extend(self.store.forks.items())
361	        contenders.sort(key=lambda item: (-len(item[1]), item[0]))

364	    def submit_fork_candidate(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
365	        """POST /v1/forks/candidates — validate and store a candidate fork.
366	
367	        Returns 201 with the fork descriptor S. Malformed or invalid forks
368	        return 400; a fork already known (identical to the canonical tip or an
369	        existing candidate tip) returns 409.
370	        """
371	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
372	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
373	        blocks_raw = payload.get("blocks")
374	        if not isinstance(blocks_raw, list):
375	            return 400, {"error": "missing field: blocks (must be a list)"}
376	        try:
377	            fork = self.store.validate_fork_blocks(blocks_raw)
378	        except ValueError as exc:
379	            return 400, {"error": str(exc)}
380	        summary = self._fork_summary(fork)
381	        # An exported fork (the five-field {tip_hash, height, length, status,
382	        # blocks} document) may be resubmitted verbatim; every supplied summary
383	        # field is re-verified against the recomputed descriptor.
384	        for field in ("tip_hash", "height", "length", "status"):
385	            if field in payload and payload[field] != summary[field]:
386	                return 400, {"error": f"summary field {field!r} does not match the blocks"}
387	        tip_hash = fork[-1].block_hash
388	        with self.store.lock:
389	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
390	            # A tip hash equal to any canonical block hash means the candidate
391	            # is exactly the canonical chain or a prefix of it (the block hash
392	            # binds height, parent and Merkle root), so it carries nothing new.
393	            if any(tip_hash == block.block_hash for block in self.store.chain):
394	                return 409, {"error": "fork is identical to the canonical chain"}
395	            if tip_hash in self.store.forks:
396	                return 409, {"error": "candidate fork already exists", "tip_hash": tip_hash}
397	            self.store.forks[tip_hash] = fork
398	            try:
399	                self.store.save()
400	            except BaseException:
401	                self.store.forks.pop(tip_hash, None)
402	                raise
403	        return 201, self._fork_summary(fork)

406	        """GET /v1/chain — canonical chain, candidates sorted by tip hash and
407	        the adoptable winner (a non-canonical chain that beats canonical).
408	        """
409	        with self.store.lock:
410	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
411	            canonical = self._fork_summary(self.store.chain)
412	            candidates = [
413	                self._fork_summary(self.store.forks[tip])
414	                for tip in sorted(self.store.forks)
415	            ]
416	            winner_tip, winner_chain = self._winning_fork()
417	            adoptable: list[dict] = []
418	            if winner_tip != self.store.tip_hash():
419	                adoptable.append(self._fork_summary(winner_chain))
420	            return 200, {
421	                "canonical": canonical,
422	                "candidates": candidates,
423	                "adoptable": adoptable,

426	    def adopt_fork(self, tip_hash: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
427	        """POST /v1/forks/{tip_hash}/adopt — atomically switch to the winner.
428	
429	        Unknown tips return 404; adopting anything other than the current
430	        winning (longest / smallest-tip-hash) chain returns 409. Adoption
431	        replaces the canonical chain and mempool in one atomic write that
432	        advances the generation and rebuilds all indexes; transactions unique
433	        to the old chain's confirmed history return to the mempool, while
434	        pending-block transactions never enter it.
435	        """
436	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tip_hash):
437	            return 404, {"error": "unknown fork tip"}
438	        with self.store.lock:
439	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
440	            fork = self.store.forks.get(tip_hash)
441	            if fork is None:
442	                return 404, {"error": "unknown fork tip"}
443	            winner_tip, _ = self._winning_fork()
444	            if winner_tip != tip_hash:
445	                return 409, {"error": "only the winning fork can be adopted"}
446	            old_chain = self.store.chain
447	            old_pending = dict(self.store.pending)
448	            self.store.forks.pop(tip_hash)
449	            self.store.replace_chain(fork)
450	            # An adopted synced tip keeps its sync records (queryable until
451	            # expiry); record the adoption once per provenance entry.
452	            adopted_keys = sorted(
453	                key
454	                for key, rec in self.store.syncs.items()
455	                if rec["tip_hash"] == tip_hash
456	            )
457	            for rec_source, request_id in adopted_keys:
458	                self.store.append_audit_event(
459	                    EVENT_SYNC_ADOPTED,
460	                    {
461	                        "source": rec_source,
462	                        "request_id": request_id,
463	                        "tip_hash": tip_hash,
464	                    },
465	                )
466	            try:
467	                self.store.save()
468	            except BaseException:
469	                # Restore the pre-adoption in-memory state on a failed write.
470	                self.store.chain = old_chain
471	                self.store.pending = old_pending
472	                self.store.forks[tip_hash] = fork
473	                self.store.rebuild_derived()
474	                del self.store.audit_events[len(self.store.audit_events) - len(adopted_keys) :]
475	                raise
476	            return 200, self._fork_summary(fork)

504	    @staticmethod
505	    def _candidate_blocks(candidate: object) -> object:
506	        """Normalize a sync ``candidate`` to its raw blocks list.
507	
508	        The candidate follows the existing export format (the five-field
509	        ``{tip_hash, height, length, status, blocks}`` document); the
510	        ``{"blocks": [...]}`` wrapper and a bare block list are accepted too.
511	        """
512	        if isinstance(candidate, dict):
513	            return candidate.get("blocks")
514	        return candidate

516	    @staticmethod
517	    def _candidate_fingerprint(blocks_raw: list) -> str:
518	        """Stable content fingerprint of a candidate's raw block list.
519	
520	        Used to decide whether a same-key retry carries the same candidate
521	        content. Key order and whitespace are normalized so two documents that
522	        serialize the same blocks identically compare equal.
523	        """
524	        return hashlib.sha256(
525	            json.dumps(blocks_raw, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
526	        ).hexdigest()

528	    def _prune_expired_syncs(self) -> list[str]:
529	        """Sweep expired sync records and persist the sweep atomically.
530	
531	        A candidate received through a sync lives only while its record is
532	        unexpired; on expiry both the record and its still-stored candidate fork
533	        are dropped, together and in a single atomic save that advances the
534	        generation. Candidates submitted directly (no sync record) never
535	        expire, and an adopted tip is no longer in ``forks`` (it is on the
536	        canonical chain), so its expiring audit record leaves the chain
537	        untouched. If the write fails the pre-cleanup records and forks are
538	        restored so no success is ever reported for an un-persisted sweep.
539	        Caller must hold the store lock. Returns the pruned tip hashes.
540	        """
541	        expired_tips, removed = self.store.prune_syncs()
542	        if not removed:
543	            return expired_tips
544	        removed_forks: dict[str, list] = {}
545	        canonical_hashes = {block.block_hash for block in self.store.chain}
546	        # The same tip could theoretically be referenced by another live
547	        # record; only drop a fork nothing still points at.
548	        live_tips = {rec["tip_hash"] for rec in self.store.syncs.values()}
549	        for tip in expired_tips:
550	            if tip in canonical_hashes or tip in live_tips:
551	                continue
552	            fork = self.store.forks.pop(tip, None)
553	            if fork is not None:
554	                removed_forks[tip] = fork
555	        # Record one permanent expiry event per removed sync record. A tip
556	        # already adopted onto the canonical chain still gets its event: the
557	        # record's expiry is auditable even though the chain is untouched.
558	        for (rec_source, request_id), rec in sorted(removed.items()):
559	            self.store.append_audit_event(
560	                EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED,
561	                {
562	                    "source": rec_source,
563	                    "request_id": request_id,
564	                    "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
565	                    "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
566	                },
567	            )
568	        try:
569	            self.store.save()
570	        except BaseException:
571	            # Restore the pre-cleanup state: a failed write must neither leave
572	            # the records gone nor their candidates orphaned, nor the events
573	            # durably visible.
574	            del self.store.audit_events[len(self.store.audit_events) - len(removed) :]
575	            self.store.restore_syncs(removed, removed_forks)
576	            raise
577	        return expired_tips

579	    def _tip_descriptor(self, tip_hash: str) -> dict | None:

582	        Looks the candidate up among stored forks first, then among canonical
583	        blocks, so audit rows remain available after the candidate is adopted.
584	        """
585	        fork = self.store.forks.get(tip_hash)
586	        if fork is not None:
587	            return self._fork_summary(fork)
588	        for block in self.store.chain:
589	            if block.block_hash == tip_hash:
590	                return {
591	                    "tip_hash": block.block_hash,
592	                    "height": block.height,
593	                    # Length counts every block including the genesis block.
594	                    "length": block.height + 1,

599	    def submit_fork_sync(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
600	        """POST /v1/forks/sync — receive a candidate chain from another node.
601	
602	        The request carries ``source``, ``request_id``, ``expires_at`` (Unix
603	        seconds) and ``candidate`` (an export-format fork document).
604	
605	        Authorization. A *new* source+request_id pair is accepted only when the
606	        source is registered in the persistent trust registry with status
607	        ``active`` and an ``expires_at`` still in the future. An unknown,
608	        revoked or registry-expired source is rejected 403 before the candidate
609	        is examined. A retry on a still-live recorded key bypasses the registry
610	        check entirely: the recorded result must keep replaying even after the
611	        source has since been rotated, revoked or expired.
612	
613	        After authorization (and only then) the candidate is re-validated
614	        exactly like a direct candidate submission (canonical genesis,
615	        consecutive heights and prev_hash linkage, recomputed block hashes and
616	        Merkle roots, tx_id and Ed25519 signatures, unique ascending tx_ids,
617	        endowment replay, pending-only-at-tip).
618	
619	        Status precedence: malformed envelope fields are 400; an unauthorized
620	        source is 403; a well-formed new request whose ``expires_at`` is not
621	        later than now is 410; a well-formed but failing candidate chain (or a
622	        tampered candidate summary) is 400. Returns 201 on first acceptance
623	        with ``{tip_hash, height, length, status, expires_at}``. A retry with
624	        the same source + request_id and identical content replays the original
625	        result as 200; the same key with different content returns 409, as does
626	        a duplicate tip already known.
627	        """
628	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
629	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
630	        for field in ("source", "request_id", "expires_at", "candidate"):
631	            if field not in payload:
632	                return 400, {"error": f"missing field: {field}"}
633	
634	        source = payload["source"]
635	        request_id = payload["request_id"]
636	        expires_at = payload["expires_at"]
637	        candidate = payload["candidate"]
638	
639	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
640	            return 400, {"error": "field 'source' must be a non-empty string"}
641	        if not isinstance(request_id, str) or not request_id:
642	            return 400, {"error": "field 'request_id' must be a non-empty string"}
643	        if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
644	            return 400, {"error": "field 'expires_at' must be a Unix-seconds integer"}
645	
646	        blocks_raw = self._candidate_blocks(candidate)
647	        if not isinstance(blocks_raw, list):
648	            return 400, {"error": "field 'candidate' must contain a 'blocks' list"}
649	
650	        with self.store.lock:
651	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
652	
653	            key = (source, request_id)
654	            existing = self.store.syncs.get(key)
655	
656	            if existing is None:
657	                # Authorization gate for new deliveries only: the source must
658	                # be an active, unexpired entry of the persistent trust
659	                # registry. Unknown, revoked or registry-expired sources are
660	                # refused 403 before the candidate is examined. A retry on a
661	                # still-live key skips this, so a recorded result keeps
662	                # replaying even after the source has since been rotated,
663	                # revoked or expired.
664	                now = time.time()
665	                trusted = self.store.trust_sources.get(source)
666	                if (
667	                    trusted is None
668	                    or trusted["status"] != TRUST_ACTIVE
669	                    or trusted["expires_at"] <= now
670	                ):
671	                    return 403, {"error": "source is not an active trusted source"}
672	                # The request's own deadline is checked next, still before the
673	                # candidate chain is examined: a well-formed request whose
674	                # expiry is not later than now is gone (410).
675	                if expires_at <= now:
676	                    return 410, {"error": "sync request has expired"}
677	
678	            # Re-validate the whole candidate chain and recompute the tip
679	            # summary BEFORE any idempotency decision: a request whose supplied
680	            # tip_hash/height/length/status were tampered with must fail 400,
681	            # never be answered with the cached 200 for its source+request_id.
682	            try:
683	                fork = self.store.validate_fork_blocks(blocks_raw)
684	            except ValueError as exc:
685	                return 400, {"error": str(exc)}
686	            summary = self._fork_summary(fork)
687	            if isinstance(candidate, dict):
688	                for field in ("tip_hash", "height", "length", "status"):
689	                    if field in candidate and candidate[field] != summary[field]:
690	                        return 400, {
691	                            "error": f"candidate field {field!r} does not match the blocks"
692	                        }
693	            tip_hash = fork[-1].block_hash
694	            # Fingerprint the *canonicalized* parsed blocks, not the raw
695	            # request list, so recovery (which re-parses the stored fork)
696	            # recomputes an identical fingerprint regardless of insignificant
697	            # serialization differences in the original submission.
698	            canonical_blocks = [block.to_dict() for block in fork]
699	            fingerprint = self._candidate_fingerprint(canonical_blocks)
700	
701	            if existing is not None:
702	                # A retry on a live key is idempotent only when it carries the
703	                # identical candidate content; a changed body conflicts 409.
704	                if fingerprint != existing["fingerprint"]:
705	                    return 409, {
706	                        "error": "request_id already used with different content"
707	                    }
708	                descriptor = self._tip_descriptor(existing["tip_hash"]) or {
709	                    "tip_hash": existing["tip_hash"],
710	                    "height": None,
711	                    "length": None,
712	                    "status": None,
713	                }
714	                return 200, {
715	                    "tip_hash": descriptor["tip_hash"],
716	                    "height": descriptor.get("height"),
717	                    "length": descriptor.get("length"),
718	                    "status": descriptor.get("status"),
719	                    "expires_at": existing["expires_at"],
720	                }
721	
722	            if any(tip_hash == block.block_hash for block in self.store.chain):
723	                return 409, {"error": "fork is identical to the canonical chain"}
724	            if tip_hash in self.store.forks:
725	                return 409, {
726	                    "error": "candidate fork already exists",
727	                    "tip_hash": tip_hash,
728	                }
729	
730	            self.store.forks[tip_hash] = fork
731	            self.store.syncs[key] = {
732	                "tip_hash": tip_hash,
733	                "expires_at": expires_at,
734	                "fingerprint": fingerprint,
735	            }
736	            self.store.append_audit_event(
737	                EVENT_SYNC_RECEIVED,
738	                {
739	                    "source": source,
740	                    "request_id": request_id,
741	                    "tip_hash": tip_hash,
742	                    "expires_at": expires_at,
743	                },
744	            )
745	            try:
746	                self.store.save()
747	            except BaseException:
748	                # Roll back the candidate, its metadata and the audit event
749	                # together so a failed write never leaves one without the others.
750	                self.store.syncs.pop(key, None)
751	                self.store.forks.pop(tip_hash, None)
752	                self.store.audit_events.pop()
753	                raise
754	
755	            result = dict(summary)
756	            result["expires_at"] = expires_at
757	            return 201, result

759	    def list_fork_syncs(self, params: dict) -> tuple[int, dict]:
760	        """GET /v1/forks/sync — audit listing of received sync candidates.
761	
762	        Filters: ``source`` (exact), ``min_height`` and ``max_height``.
763	        ``limit`` defaults to 50 and must be 1-200; ``cursor`` defaults to 0.
764	        Every numeric value must be a plain decimal without leading zeros; a
765	        malformed value returns 400. Rows are ordered by
766	        ``(height, tip_hash, source)``; ``cursor == total`` returns an empty
767	        page, ``cursor > total`` returns 400. Each item carries
768	        ``source, request_id, tip_hash, height, length, status, expires_at``.
769	        """

771	        if source is not None and (not isinstance(source, str) or not source):
772	            return 400, {"error": "source must be a non-empty string"}
773	
774	        min_height = None
775	        if params.get("min_height") is not None:
776	            min_height = _parse_decimal(params["min_height"])
777	            if min_height is None:
778	                return 400, {"error": "min_height must be a non-negative decimal"}
779	        max_height = None
780	        if params.get("max_height") is not None:
781	            max_height = _parse_decimal(params["max_height"])
782	            if max_height is None:
783	                return 400, {"error": "max_height must be a non-negative decimal"}
784	        if min_height is not None and max_height is not None and min_height > max_height:
785	            return 400, {"error": "min_height must not exceed max_height"}
786	
787	        limit = self.SYNC_DEFAULT_LIMIT
788	        if params.get("limit") is not None:
789	            parsed = _parse_decimal(params["limit"])
790	            if parsed is None or not 1 <= parsed <= self.SYNC_MAX_LIMIT:
791	                return 400, {"error": "limit must be a decimal between 1 and 200"}
792	            limit = parsed
793	        cursor = 0
794	        if params.get("cursor") is not None:
795	            parsed = _parse_decimal(params["cursor"])
796	            if parsed is None:
797	                return 400, {"error": "cursor must be a non-negative decimal"}
798	            cursor = parsed
799	
800	        with self.store.lock:
801	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
802	            rows: list[dict] = []
803	            for (rec_source, request_id), rec in self.store.syncs.items():
804	                if source is not None and rec_source != source:
805	                    continue
806	                descriptor = self._tip_descriptor(rec["tip_hash"])
807	                if descriptor is None:
808	                    continue
809	                if min_height is not None and descriptor["height"] < min_height:
810	                    continue
811	                if max_height is not None and descriptor["height"] > max_height:
812	                    continue
813	                rows.append(
814	                    {
815	                        "source": rec_source,
816	                        "request_id": request_id,
817	                        "tip_hash": descriptor["tip_hash"],
818	                        "height": descriptor["height"],
819	                        "length": descriptor["length"],
820	                        "status": descriptor["status"],
821	                        "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
822	                    }
823	                )
824	
825	        rows.sort(key=lambda row: (row["height"], row["tip_hash"], row["source"]))
826	        total = len(rows)
827	        if cursor > total:
828	            return 400, {"error": "cursor is beyond the result set"}
829	        items = rows[cursor : cursor + limit]
830	        next_cursor = cursor + limit if cursor + limit < total else None
831	        return 200, {"items": items, "total": total, "next_cursor": next_cursor}

839	    def list_transactions(self, params: dict) -> tuple[int, dict]:
840	        """GET /v1/index/transactions — paginated confirmed-chain tx index.

842	        Pending-tip transactions are excluded. Filters (AND-combined):
843	        ``tx_id`` (64 lowercase hex), ``account`` (matches sender or
844	        recipient) and ``height``; ``limit`` (default 50, range 1-200) and
845	        ``cursor`` (default 0) paginate. Numeric filters must be plain
846	        decimals without leading zeros; any malformed value returns 400.

848	        transaction's 0-based position inside its block, matching the Merkle
849	        proof index. A cursor beyond the filtered total returns 400, a cursor
850	        equal to it returns an empty page.
851	        """
852	        tx_id = params.get("tx_id")
853	        if tx_id is not None and not crypto.is_hex64(tx_id):
854	            return 400, {"error": "tx_id must be 64 lowercase hex characters"}
855	        account = params.get("account")
856	        if account is not None and (not isinstance(account, str) or not account):
857	            return 400, {"error": "account must be a non-empty string"}
858	
859	        height = None
860	        if params.get("height") is not None:
861	            height = _parse_decimal(params["height"])
862	            if height is None:
863	                return 400, {"error": "height must be a non-negative decimal"}
864	        limit = self.INDEX_DEFAULT_LIMIT
865	        if params.get("limit") is not None:
866	            parsed = _parse_decimal(params["limit"])
867	            if parsed is None or not 1 <= parsed <= self.INDEX_MAX_LIMIT:
868	                return 400, {"error": "limit must be a decimal between 1 and 200"}
869	            limit = parsed
870	        cursor = 0
871	        if params.get("cursor") is not None:
872	            parsed = _parse_decimal(params["cursor"])
873	            if parsed is None:
874	                return 400, {"error": "cursor must be a non-negative decimal"}
875	            cursor = parsed
876	
877	        with self.store.lock:
878	            rows: list[dict] = []
879	            for block in self.store.chain:
880	                if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
881	                    continue
882	                if height is not None and block.height != height:
883	                    continue
884	                for index, tx in enumerate(block.transactions):
885	                    if tx_id is not None and tx.tx_id != tx_id:
886	                        continue
887	                    if account is not None and account not in (tx.sender, tx.recipient):
888	                        continue
889	                    rows.append(
890	                        {
891	                            "tx_id": tx.tx_id,
892	                            "height": block.height,
893	                            "block_hash": block.block_hash,
894	                            "index": index,
895	                            "from": tx.sender,
896	                            "to": tx.recipient,
897	                            "amount": tx.amount,
898	                        }
899	                    )
900	        # Chain order is already (height, index) ascending; the tx_id
901	        # tiebreaker is implied because ids are unique within a block.
902	        total = len(rows)
903	        if cursor > total:
904	            return 400, {"error": "cursor is beyond the result set"}
905	        items = rows[cursor : cursor + limit]
906	        next_cursor = cursor + limit if cursor + limit < total else None
907	        return 200, {"items": items, "total": total, "next_cursor": next_cursor}

912	    def _trust_record(source: str, rec: dict) -> dict:
913	        """Public shape of one trust-source record."""
914	        return {
915	            "source": source,
916	            "public_key": rec["public_key"],

922	    def _validate_trust_input(self, payload: object, require_version: bool) -> tuple | None:
923	        """Validate a trust registration/rotation body.
924	
925	        ``source`` must be a non-empty string, ``public_key`` 64 lowercase
926	        hex characters and ``expires_at`` a plain (non-boolean) integer.
927	        Rotation/revocation additionally require a positive integer
928	        ``expected_version``. Returns (source, public_key, expires_at[,
929	        expected_version]) or None after sending a 400.
930	        """
931	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
932	            return None
933	        for field in ("source", "public_key", "expires_at"):
934	            if field not in payload:
935	                return None
936	        source = payload["source"]
937	        public_key = payload["public_key"]
938	        expires_at = payload["expires_at"]
939	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
940	            return None
941	        if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
942	            return None
943	        if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
944	            return None
945	        if not require_version:
946	            return source, public_key, expires_at
947	        expected_version = payload.get("expected_version")
948	        if (
949	            isinstance(expected_version, bool)
950	            or not isinstance(expected_version, int)
951	            or expected_version < 1
952	        ):
953	            return None
954	        return source, public_key, expires_at, expected_version

956	    def register_trust_source(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
957	        """POST /v1/trust/sources — register a trusted source.
958	
959	        A new source is created at version 1 with status ``active`` and the
960	        change is persisted together with its audit event in one atomic write
961	        (201). Re-posting the exact same (public_key, expires_at) content is
962	        idempotent (200, the stored record unchanged); the same source with
963	        different content conflicts (409).
964	        """
965	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
966	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
967	        for field in ("source", "public_key", "expires_at"):
968	            if field not in payload:
969	                return 400, {"error": f"missing field: {field}"}
970	        parsed = self._validate_trust_input(payload, require_version=False)
971	        if parsed is None:
972	            return 400, {
973	                "error": "source must be a non-empty string, public_key 64 "
974	                "lowercase hex characters and expires_at an integer"
975	            }
976	        source, public_key, expires_at = parsed
977	        with self.store.lock:
978	            existing = self.store.trust_sources.get(source)
979	            if existing is not None:
980	                if (
981	                    existing["public_key"] == public_key
982	                    and existing["expires_at"] == expires_at
983	                ):
984	                    # Idempotent re-registration: the stored record is reported
985	                    # unchanged, with no new version and no new audit event.
986	                    return 200, self._trust_record(source, existing)
987	                return 409, {"error": "trust source already exists with different content"}
988	            record = {
989	                "public_key": public_key,
990	                "expires_at": expires_at,
991	                "version": 1,
992	                "status": TRUST_ACTIVE,
993	            }
994	            self.store.trust_sources[source] = record
995	            self.store.append_audit_event(
996	                EVENT_SOURCE_REGISTERED,
997	                {
998	                    "source": source,
999	                    "public_key": public_key,
1000	                    "expires_at": expires_at,
1001	                    "version": 1,
1002	                },
1003	            )
1004	            try:
1005	                self.store.save()
1006	            except BaseException:
1007	                # Undo both the registry change and its event together.
1008	                self.store.trust_sources.pop(source, None)
1009	                self.store.audit_events.pop()
1010	                raise
1011	            return 201, self._trust_record(source, record)

1013	    def rotate_trust_source(self, source: object, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
1014	        """POST /v1/trust/sources/{source}/rotate — install a new public key.
1015	
1016	        Requires ``public_key``, ``expires_at`` and ``expected_version``. An
1017	        unknown or already-revoked source returns 404; a stale
1018	        ``expected_version`` returns 409. A successful rotation increments the
1019	        version, keeps the source active and persists the change with an audit
1020	        event atomically.
1021	        """
1022	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
1023	            return 404, {"error": "unknown trust source"}
1024	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
1025	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
1026	        for field in ("public_key", "expires_at", "expected_version"):
1027	            if field not in payload:
1028	                return 400, {"error": f"missing field: {field}"}
1029	        body = dict(payload)
1030	        body["source"] = source
1031	        parsed = self._validate_trust_input(body, require_version=True)
1032	        if parsed is None:
1033	            return 400, {
1034	                "error": "public_key must be 64 lowercase hex characters and "
1035	                "expires_at/expected_version integers"
1036	            }
1037	        _, public_key, expires_at, expected_version = parsed
1038	        with self.store.lock:
1039	            existing = self.store.trust_sources.get(source)
1040	            if existing is None or existing["status"] == TRUST_REVOKED:
1041	                return 404, {"error": "unknown trust source"}
1042	            if existing["version"] != expected_version:
1043	                return 409, {"error": "expected_version does not match the current version"}
1044	            old_record = dict(existing)
1045	            existing["public_key"] = public_key
1046	            existing["expires_at"] = expires_at
1047	            existing["version"] = old_record["version"] + 1
1048	            self.store.append_audit_event(
1049	                EVENT_SOURCE_ROTATED,
1050	                {
1051	                    "source": source,
1052	                    "public_key": public_key,
1053	                    "expires_at": expires_at,
1054	                    "version": existing["version"],
1055	                },
1056	            )
1057	            try:
1058	                self.store.save()
1059	            except BaseException:
1060	                self.store.trust_sources[source] = old_record
1061	                self.store.audit_events.pop()
1062	                raise
1063	            return 200, self._trust_record(source, existing)

1066	        """POST /v1/trust/sources/{source}/revoke — revoke a trusted source.

1069	        version mismatch returns 409; revoking an already-revoked source at the
1070	        recorded version is idempotent (200). A new revocation marks the source
1071	        revoked and is persisted with its audit event atomically.
1072	        """
1073	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
1074	            return 404, {"error": "unknown trust source"}
1075	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
1076	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
1077	        if "expected_version" not in payload:
1078	            return 400, {"error": "missing field: expected_version"}
1079	        expected_version = payload["expected_version"]
1080	        if (
1081	            isinstance(expected_version, bool)
1082	            or not isinstance(expected_version, int)
1083	            or expected_version < 1
1084	        ):
1085	            return 400, {"error": "expected_version must be a positive integer"}

1087	            existing = self.store.trust_sources.get(source)
1088	            if existing is None:

1094	                return 200, self._trust_record(source, existing)

1096	            existing["status"] = TRUST_REVOKED

1098	                EVENT_SOURCE_REVOKED,
1099	                {
1100	                    "source": source,
1101	                    "public_key": existing["public_key"],
1102	                    "expires_at": existing["expires_at"],
1103	                    "version": existing["version"],
1104	                },
1105	            )
1106	            try:
1107	                self.store.save()
1108	            except BaseException:
1109	                existing["status"] = old_status
1110	                self.store.audit_events.pop()
1111	                raise

1	"""Persistent storage: blockchain, pending set and derived indexes (JSON).
2	
3	The whole state is one JSON document written atomically: a uniquely named
4	``.ledger-*`` snapshot is fsynced in the same directory and then promoted over
5	the main file with ``os.replace`` (followed by a directory fsync). Every
6	successful write advances a monotonic ``generation`` recorded in the
7	snapshot. A crash can therefore only leave behind (a) the previous main file
8	or (b) a fully fsynced snapshot that never got renamed — never a torn file.
9	
10	On startup the main file and every sibling ``.ledger-*`` snapshot are treated
11	as recovery candidates. When no file exists at all, the unique genesis block
12	is created; otherwise each candidate is strictly validated (JSON, generation,
13	consecutive heights, prev_hash linkage, recomputed block hashes and Merkle
14	roots, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signature, pending-only-at-tip and
15	mempool/chain de-duplication). The valid snapshot with the highest generation
16	wins and is promoted if it is still a temp file; same-generation content
17	conflicts, or a directory with no valid candidate, raise StateRecoveryError
18	with the offending path and reason — a fresh chain is never silently created.
19	
20	One atomic write persists everything: the chain (each block carries its
21	confirm/rollback ``status``), a small ``state`` summary, the mempool
22	(``pending``), candidate fork chains (``forks``, each a full block list
23	anchored at the canonical genesis and keyed by its tip hash), the
24	confirmed-transaction ``index`` and the confirmed ``accounts`` activity.
25	Derived data (index/accounts) is *rebuilt* from the chain on every load and
26	every save — pending blocks are excluded, so a restart never resurrects
27	unconfirmed transactions into balances. Persisted fork candidates are
28	re-validated on startup and invalid ones are dropped, while canonical-chain
29	invalidity remains fatal. Persisted sync records are re-verified on restart:
30	records still unexpired whose source stays active and unexpired survive;
31	records whose own deadline elapsed or whose source is unknown/revoked/
32	registry-expired while the process was down are pruned (their non-adopted
33	forks removed; an adopted tip never changes the canonical chain) and each
34	gets exactly one sync_expired audit event backfilled after the durable
35	history, persisted in one atomic write. The backfill deduplicates only
36	within the record's current lifecycle (a durable sync_expired newer than
37	the key's latest sync_received), so a reused (source, request_id) key's
38	new lifecycle is always audited even when every field matches a previous
39	lifecycle's event. Other staleness (a dangling
40	tip or a content-fingerprint mismatch) is a silent prune with no event.
41	A re-entrant lock serializes all updates, and a class-wide recovery lock
42	serializes startup scans against in-flight writes.
43	"""

539	        # Cross-check the persisted tip summary against the chain tail.
540	        tip = chain[-1]
541	        if state.get("height") is not None and state["height"] != tip.height:
542	            fail("state.height does not match the chain tip")
543	        if state.get("tip_hash") is not None and state["tip_hash"] != tip.block_hash:
544	            fail("state.tip_hash does not match the chain tip")
545	        if (
546	            state.get("tip_status") is not None
547	            and state["tip_status"] != tip.status
548	        ):
549	            fail("state.tip_status does not match the chain tip")
550	
551	        # The recorded endowment is the *only* balance-replay parameter for the
552	        # persisted fork candidates: revalidation below must use it rather than
553	        # this instance's constructor argument, so starting with a different
554	        # --initial-balance can never change a fork's legality. Only a legacy
555	        # snapshot that records no endowment falls back to the configured (then
556	        # the default) value; every snapshot written by current code records it.
557	        replay_endowment = initial_balance
558	        if replay_endowment is None:
559	            replay_endowment = (
560	                self.initial_balance
561	                if self.initial_balance is not None
562	                else DEFAULT_INITIAL_BALANCE
563	            )
564	
565	        forks = self._parse_persisted_forks(
566	            data.get("forks", []), chain, replay_endowment
567	        )
568	        # The trust registry is authoritative configuration and must be parsed
569	        # before the sync records, whose sources are re-authorized against it.
570	        trust_sources = self._parse_persisted_trust_sources(
571	            data.get("trust_sources", []), path
572	        )
573	        # Parse the durable append-only audit log verbatim. It must NOT be
574	        # mutated here: same-generation snapshot conflict detection compares
575	        # parsed audit events, and a time-dependent backfill would make two
576	        # byte-identical snapshots look conflicting. The expired-record
577	        # reconciliation returned below is applied once, by load(), to the
578	        # single winning snapshot.
579	        audit_events = self._parse_persisted_audit_events(
580	            data.get("audit_events", []), path
581	        )
582	        syncs, expired_records, synced_tips = self._parse_persisted_syncs(
583	            data.get("syncs", []), forks, chain, trust_sources
584	        )
585	        # A fork brought in only by a sync record loses its right to exist once
586	        # that record is gone (expired/unauthorized/invalid on restart):
587	        # without this, the independently-persisted fork would resurrect as a
588	        # never-expiring candidate. Direct submissions carry no sync record and
589	        # are untouched.
590	        live_tips = {rec["tip_hash"] for rec in syncs.values()}
591	        canonical_hashes = {block.block_hash for block in chain}
592	        for tip in synced_tips - live_tips - canonical_hashes:
593	            forks.pop(tip, None)
594	        allowlist = self._parse_persisted_allowlist(data.get("allowlist", {}), path)
595	        return (
596	            chain,
597	            pending,
598	            generation,
599	            forks,
600	            initial_balance,
601	            syncs,
602	            trust_sources,
603	            allowlist,
604	            audit_events,
605	            expired_records,
606	        )

608	    @staticmethod
609	    def _backfill_expired_events(
610	        audit_events: list[dict],
611	        expired_records: list[tuple[str, str, dict]],
612	    ) -> int:
613	        """Append one sync_expired event per down-time-expired sync record.
614	
615	        Mirrors the runtime sweep exactly: records are processed in
616	        ``(source, request_id)`` order, each gets a dense event_id continuing
617	        after the durable history, and every *lifecycle removal* gets its own
618	        event. Deduplication is lifecycle-aware, never identity-based across
619	        lifecycles: a durable sync_expired covers the persisted record only
620	        when it sits after the latest sync_received for the same
621	        ``(source, request_id)`` key — i.e. it belongs to the record's
622	        current lifecycle (the crash-interrupted-cleanup case). An expiry
623	        event from an *earlier* lifecycle of a reused key never suppresses
624	        the new lifecycle's event, even when source, request_id, tip_hash
625	        and expires_at are all identical. Returns the number of events
626	        appended. Mutates ``audit_events`` in place.
627	        """
628	        # Position of the latest sync_received per key: it opens the
629	        # lifecycle every later event of that key belongs to.
630	        last_received: dict[tuple[object, object], int] = {}
631	        for index, event in enumerate(audit_events):
632	            if event.get("kind") == EVENT_SYNC_RECEIVED:
633	                last_received[(event.get("source"), event.get("request_id"))] = index
634	        # Identities already expired *within their current lifecycle*.
635	        covered: set[tuple[object, object, object]] = set()
636	        for index, event in enumerate(audit_events):
637	            if event.get("kind") != EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED:
638	                continue
639	            key = (event.get("source"), event.get("request_id"))
640	            if index > last_received.get(key, -1):
641	                covered.add((key[0], key[1], event.get("tip_hash")))
642	        backfilled = 0
643	        for source, request_id, rec in sorted(
644	            expired_records, key=lambda item: (item[0], item[1])
645	        ):
646	            identity = (source, request_id, rec["tip_hash"])
647	            if identity in covered:
648	                continue
649	            audit_events.append(
650	                {
651	                    "event_id": len(audit_events) + 1,
652	                    "kind": EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED,
653	                    "at": time.time(),
654	                    "source": source,
655	                    "request_id": request_id,
656	                    "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
657	                    "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
658	                }
659	            )
660	            covered.add(identity)
661	            backfilled += 1
662	        return backfilled

664	    @staticmethod
665	    def _parse_persisted_trust_sources(
666	        raw: object, path: str
667	    ) -> dict[str, dict]:
668	        """Strictly parse the persisted source-trust registry.
669	
670	        Unlike candidate forks (re-validated and silently dropped when stale),
671	        the trust registry is authoritative configuration: a malformed entry
672	        is snapshot corruption and fails recovery rather than being dropped.
673	        Each record needs a non-empty source, a 64-char lowercase hex public
674	        key, an integer expiry, a positive integer version and a known status.
675	        """
676	        if raw is None:
677	            return {}
678	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
679	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "'trust_sources' must be a list")
680	        sources: dict[str, dict] = {}
681	        for entry in raw:
682	            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
683	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, "trust source entry must be an object")
684	            source = entry.get("source")
685	            public_key = entry.get("public_key")
686	            expires_at = entry.get("expires_at")
687	            version = entry.get("version")
688	            status = entry.get("status")
689	            if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
690	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, "trust source must be a non-empty string")
691	            if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
692	                raise StateRecoveryError(
693	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} has an invalid public_key"
694	                )
695	            if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
696	                raise StateRecoveryError(
697	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} expires_at must be an integer"
698	                )
699	            if (
700	                isinstance(version, bool)
701	                or not isinstance(version, int)
702	                or version < 1
703	            ):
704	                raise StateRecoveryError(
705	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} version must be a positive integer"
706	                )
707	            if status not in (TRUST_ACTIVE, TRUST_REVOKED):
708	                raise StateRecoveryError(
709	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} has invalid status {status!r}"
710	                )
711	            if source in sources:
712	                raise StateRecoveryError(
713	                    path, f"duplicate trust source {source!r} in snapshot"
714	                )
715	            sources[source] = {
716	                "public_key": public_key,
717	                "expires_at": expires_at,
718	                "version": version,
719	                "status": status,
720	            }
721	        return sources

724	    def _parse_persisted_allowlist(raw: object, path: str) -> dict[str, int]:
725	        """Strictly parse the keyless ``{source: expires_at}`` allowlist."""
726	        if raw is None:
727	            return {}
728	        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
729	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "'allowlist' must be a JSON object")
730	        allowlist: dict[str, int] = {}
731	        for source, expires_at in raw.items():
732	            if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
733	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, "allowlist source must be a non-empty string")

741	    @staticmethod
742	    def _parse_persisted_audit_events(raw: object, path: str) -> list[dict]:
743	        """Strictly parse the append-only audit event log.
744	
745	        Every event is a JSON object carrying an integer ``at`` timestamp and a
746	        string ``kind``; ``event_id`` values must be exactly 1..N with no gaps
747	        or duplicates, since the id is the event's permanent audit position.
748	        Payload fields beyond those three are retained verbatim.
749	        """
750	        if raw is None:
751	            return []
752	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
753	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "'audit_events' must be a list")
754	        events: list[dict] = []
755	        for i, event in enumerate(raw):
756	            if not isinstance(event, dict):
757	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"audit event {i + 1} must be an object")
758	            event_id = event.get("event_id")
759	            kind = event.get("kind")
760	            at = event.get("at")
761	            if (
762	                isinstance(event_id, bool)
763	                or not isinstance(event_id, int)
764	                or event_id != i + 1
765	            ):
766	                raise StateRecoveryError(
767	                    path,
768	                    f"audit event at position {i} has event_id {event_id!r}, "
769	                    f"expected {i + 1}",
770	                )
771	            if not isinstance(kind, str) or not kind:
772	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"audit event {event_id} needs a kind")
773	            if isinstance(at, bool) or not isinstance(at, (int, float)):
774	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"audit event {event_id} needs a numeric 'at'")
775	            events.append(dict(event))
776	        return events

778	    def _parse_persisted_syncs(
779	        self,
780	        syncs_raw: object,
781	        forks: dict[str, list[Block]],
782	        canonical_chain: list[Block],
783	        trust_sources: dict[str, dict] | None = None,
784	    ) -> tuple[dict[tuple[str, str], dict], list[tuple[str, str, dict]], set[str]]:
785	        """Parse persisted sync records, dropping unusable ones on restart.
786	
787	        A record is kept only when it is structurally valid, has not yet
788	        expired, its source is still an active, unexpired entry of the
789	        persistent trust registry, and its tip references either a surviving
790	        candidate fork or a block on the canonical chain (a synced candidate
791	        may have been adopted). Records that expire while the process is down,
792	        or whose source is unknown/revoked/registry-expired, are pruned and
793	        additionally returned as ``expired_records`` (each as
794	        ``(source, request_id, {tip_hash, expires_at, fingerprint})``) so the
795	        caller backfills one sync_expired audit event per record — mirroring
796	        the runtime sweep. Other staleness (malformed structure, a record
797	        pointing at neither surviving location, or a fingerprint that no
798	        longer matches the delivered candidate) is a silent orphan prune with
799	        no event; duplicated keys keep the first copy. Invalid records are
800	        silently dropped rather than failing recovery of the canonical chain.
801	        The historical sync_received/sync_adopted/sync_expired audit events
802	        are never touched by this pruning. Also returns the set of every tip
803	        any sync record claims provenance for (including dropped ones), so the
804	        caller can drop forks that only a pruned sync kept alive.
805	        """
806	        if not isinstance(syncs_raw, list):
807	            return {}, [], set()
808	        now = time.time()
809	        trust_sources = trust_sources or {}
810	        # Map every canonical block hash to the chain prefix ending there:
811	        # this is the exact "candidate" document that was delivered for a tip
812	        # since adopted onto the canonical chain.
813	        canonical_prefixes: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
814	        prefix: list[dict] = []
815	        for block in canonical_chain:
816	            prefix = prefix + [block.to_dict()]
817	            canonical_prefixes[block.block_hash] = prefix
818	        syncs: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
819	        expired_records: list[tuple[str, str, dict]] = []
820	        synced_tips: set[str] = set()
821	        for rec_raw in syncs_raw:
822	            if not isinstance(rec_raw, dict):
823	                continue
824	            source = rec_raw.get("source")
825	            request_id = rec_raw.get("request_id")
826	            tip_hash = rec_raw.get("tip_hash")
827	            expires_at = rec_raw.get("expires_at")
828	            fingerprint = rec_raw.get("fingerprint")
829	            if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
830	                continue
831	            if not isinstance(request_id, str) or not request_id:
832	                continue
833	            if not crypto.is_hex64(tip_hash):
834	                continue
835	            # Provenance is recorded even for dropped records: it proves the
836	            # matching fork must not outlive the sync that delivered it.
837	            synced_tips.add(tip_hash)
838	            record = {
839	                "tip_hash": tip_hash,
840	                "expires_at": expires_at,
841	                "fingerprint": fingerprint,
842	            }
843	            if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
844	                # Malformed deadline: a structurally broken record, silently
845	                # pruned (no lifecycle event is attributable to it).
846	                continue
847	            expired_deadline = expires_at <= now
848	            # Re-authorization on restart: the trust decision recorded at
849	            # delivery is re-checked against the current registry. A source
850	            # rotated away, revoked or expired since then invalidates its
851	            # pending records; historical audit events stay queryable.
852	            trusted = trust_sources.get(source)
853	            auth_ok = (
854	                trusted is not None
855	                and trusted.get("status") == TRUST_ACTIVE
856	                and isinstance(trusted.get("expires_at"), int)
857	                and not isinstance(trusted.get("expires_at"), bool)
858	                and trusted["expires_at"] > now
859	            )
860	            if expired_deadline or not auth_ok:
861	                # Deadline elapsed or authorization lost while down: reconcile
862	                # exactly like the runtime sweep and backfill sync_expired,
863	                # regardless of the content fingerprint (the lifecycle event
864	                # is identified by source/request_id/tip/expires_at).
865	                expired_records.append((source, request_id, record))
866	                continue
867	            if not isinstance(fingerprint, str) or not fingerprint:
868	                continue
869	            # Re-resolve the delivered candidate (a surviving fork, or the
870	            # canonical prefix for an adopted tip) and recompute its content
871	            # fingerprint: a tampered tip summary, deadline or request body
872	            # must not be trusted on the strength of the persisted record.
873	            blocks_raw: list[dict] | None = None
874	            surviving_fork = forks.get(tip_hash)
875	            if surviving_fork is not None:
876	                blocks_raw = [block.to_dict() for block in surviving_fork]
877	            else:
878	                blocks_raw = canonical_prefixes.get(tip_hash)
879	            if blocks_raw is None:
880	                continue
881	            if self._candidate_fingerprint(blocks_raw) != fingerprint:
882	                continue
883	            key = (source, request_id)
884	            if key in syncs:
885	                continue
886	            syncs[key] = {
887	                "tip_hash": tip_hash,
888	                "expires_at": expires_at,
889	                "fingerprint": fingerprint,
890	            }
891	        return syncs, expired_records, synced_tips

893	    @staticmethod
894	    def _candidate_fingerprint(blocks_raw: list) -> str:
895	        """Stable SHA-256 content fingerprint of a candidate's raw block list.
896	
897	        Mirrors ``LedgerService._candidate_fingerprint`` so recovery can check
898	        the persisted record against the re-parsed candidate without importing
899	        the service layer. Key order and whitespace are normalized.
900	        """
901	        return hashlib.sha256(
902	            json.dumps(blocks_raw, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
903	        ).hexdigest()

940	    def _compute_derived(self) -> tuple[dict[str, int], dict[str, dict]]:
941	        """Build the confirmed-only transaction index and account activity.
942	
943	        Pending blocks are excluded: only confirmed blocks contribute to
944	        balances and to the tx_id -> height index. Pure: it returns fresh
945	        dicts and never mutates store state, so callers can compute a
946	        prospective view and publish it only after a successful write.
947	        """
948	        tx_index: dict[str, int] = {}
949	        accounts: dict[str, dict] = {}
950	        for block in self.chain:
951	            if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
952	                continue
953	            for tx in block.transactions:
954	                tx_index[tx.tx_id] = block.height
955	                for account in (tx.sender, tx.recipient):
956	                    entry = accounts.setdefault(
957	                        account, {"sent": 0, "received": 0, "transactions": []}
958	                    )
959	                    entry["transactions"].append(tx.tx_id)
960	                accounts[tx.sender]["sent"] += tx.amount
961	                accounts[tx.recipient]["received"] += tx.amount
962	        return tx_index, accounts

966	
967	        Pending blocks are excluded: only confirmed blocks contribute to
968	        balances and to the tx_id -> height index.
969	        """
970	        self.tx_index, self.accounts = self._compute_derived()
